issues.detail: The Vietnamese translation adds the word 'Nguyền' (Curse/May it be) at the beginning of both clauses. The Greek text is a standard blessing (optative/imperative sense) and does not contain any word corresponding to a curse or 'nguyền'.

The Vietnamese rendering of 'το πνευμα' as 'tâm thần' is a conceptual shift. While 'tâm thần' can relate to spirit/mind, the Greek 'πνεύμα' is specifically 'spirit'. In this context, 'tâm thần' might imply 'mental state' or 'sanity' more than 'spirit'.
